author: J. W. Yates
title: Walter Hudson raises concerns over election integrity and transgender athlete policies
text:
Walter Hudson, a Minnesota state representative, posted a series of tweets on March 18, 2026, addressing issues related to transgender participation in sports and election integrity.
In a tweet published at 02:00 UTC, Hudson referenced his prior comments during a committee hearing about the participation of boys in girls’ sports. He stated: “A year ago, I offered comment in a committee hearing about boys playing in girl’s sports.. Self-identified ‘queer’ Democrats got up and walked out rather than explain how I was wrong… … because they couldn’t. “.
Later that day at 18:29 UTC, Hudson questioned the implications of removing non-citizens from voter rolls. He wrote: “If ‘almost no illegal immigrants vote,’ what harm comes from removing those who do from the rolls?”.
At 18:40 UTC on the same day, Hudson commented on Alaska’s role regarding proposed federal election legislation known as SAVE America. He asserted: “Alaska could make changes to adapt and make SAVE America work. Their internal challenges should not hold up a bill that 80% of Americans support. 10s of 1000s of illegible registrations have already be identified. It’s obvious where the urgency should be.”
Election integrity has been an ongoing topic across U.S. states, with various proposals aiming to address concerns over voter registration accuracy and eligibility verification. Public opinion polls have shown broad support for measures requiring proof of citizenship for voting eligibility.
Debates over transgender athletes’ participation in school sports have also intensified nationwide, with legislatures considering or enacting laws restricting such participation based on sex assigned at birth.
